title: Skillet Apple Crisp with Almonds
summary: Apples browned in butter in a frying pan, glossed with reduced apple juice and baked under an almond and oat topping.
equipment: 30 cm ovenproof frying pan (cast iron or stainless)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
firm, sweet apples (such as Braeburn or Golden Delicious), peeled, cored and cut in 1.5 cm wedges

steps.title: Mix the topping
steps.text: Stir the flour, almonds, oats, both sugars, cinnamon and salt together, then drizzle in the melted butter and toss until evenly moist and clumpy. Set aside.

steps.title: Reduce the juice
steps.text: Simmer the apple juice in the small saucepan until reduced to about 120 ml, 6-8 minutes. Concentrated juice adds deep apple flavour without making the filling wet.

steps.title: Brown the apples
steps.text: Toss the apples with the 50 g sugar and the cinnamon. Melt the 30 g butter in the frying pan over a medium-high heat and cook the apples, stirring now and then, for 12-14 minutes until browned on the outside and just tender inside.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and stir in the reduced juice and the lemon juice so the apples are glossy.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Scatter the topping evenly over the apples, set the pan on a baking tray and bake 12-15 minutes, until the topping is a deep golden brown and the juices bubble. Rest 15 minutes before serving.

tips: Choose apples that hold their shape, such as Braeburn, Jazz or Golden Delicious.
A common mistake is crowding a small pan, which steams the apples instead of browning them.
Use cloudy apple juice for the fullest flavour.
Watch the topping in the hot oven; almonds go from golden to burnt quickly.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat in the oven to keep the topping crisp.
